test_cases.name: Basic Framework Carousel Creation
test_cases.description: User wants to create a carousel about a business framework they use
test_cases.prompt: Help me create a LinkedIn carousel about the 5-step process I use to evaluate SaaS tools for my team. The goal is to build authority and get people to save it for reference.
expected_outputs: Should suggest framework-based narrative structure
Should ask clarifying questions about: the 5 steps, target audience, desired CTA
Should provide slide outline (7 slides optimal)
Should include hook formula recommendation
Should reference design specs (1080x1350px portrait)
Should explain why this content type drives saves
Should provide caption formula matching the framework approach
success_criteria: Provides concrete slide-by-slide outline with suggested headlines
Hooks are specific and promise clear value
References 2026 engagement data (frameworks are saveable content type)
Includes step count guidance (5-10 slides, 7 optimal)
Mentions mobile-first design considerations
Provides export/posting workflow

test_cases.name: Contrarian Argument Carousel
test_cases.description: User wants to create a contrarian carousel challenging conventional wisdom
test_cases.prompt: I want to post a LinkedIn carousel arguing that daily posting actually hurts engagement, not helps it. How do I structure this to get people commenting and engaging?
expected_outputs: Should suggest contrarian/argument-based narrative structure
Should explain why controversial content drives comments
Should provide hook formula for contradiction/challenge
Should include data-backed approach (stats, evidence)
Should warn about avoiding engagement bait vs substance
Should provide slide structure that builds the argument progressively
Should reference algorithm signals for comment-driving content
success_criteria: Provides specific structure: Claim → Evidence → Counter-argument → Data → Implication
Includes evidence-based arguments (references research data)
Hook is provocative but backed by substance
Explains why this content type drives comments (high-engagement signal)
Provides checklist for avoiding 'engagement bait' feeling
Includes CTA designed for comments, not just saves

test_cases.name: Personal Narrative Carousel
test_cases.description: User wants to share a personal story with professional lessons
test_cases.prompt: I left a $200K job to start a startup. I want to create a carousel about the unexpected lessons I learned. Will this format work well, and how should I structure it?
expected_outputs: Should confirm personal narrative is high-engagement format
Should provide 7-slide structure for narrative arc
Should explain how to extract universal lessons from personal story
Should include hook formula for surprising outcome
Should address authenticity and relatability
Should provide design guidance for narrative flow (visual progression)
Should include engagement metrics for this content type
success_criteria: Provides narrative arc: Hook (outcome) → Story (2-4 slides) → Insight → Application → CTA
Explains how to make personal lessons generalizable (not just one-off story)
Includes hook formula emphasizing surprising outcome
References authenticity as signal (algorithm favors genuine content)
Slide count guidance appropriate for narrative (6-8 slides typical)
Design advice on visual consistency for story progression

test_cases.name: Design & Technical Specifications
test_cases.description: User has content outline and needs technical guidance for design
test_cases.prompt: I've outlined my carousel but I'm using Canva. What dimensions should I use, and what's the right way to export it for LinkedIn? Any design rules I should follow?
expected_outputs: Should recommend 1080 x 1350px (portrait, 4:5 ratio) with explanation
Should explain why portrait is optimal (mobile engagement)
Should provide font sizing rules (24px+ body, 36px+ headlines)
Should explain color strategy (2 fonts, 3 colors max)
Should provide export checklist (PDF Standard, not PDF Print)
Should reference mobile readability (67% traffic from mobile)
Should include contrast/high-visibility requirements
success_criteria: Recommends portrait (1080x1350) with specific reason (mobile engagement, 60%+ mobile users)
Explains why portrait > square > landscape by engagement data
Provides font sizing minimums backed by readability research
Color palette guidance (not rainbow, high contrast required)
Specific Canva export instructions (PDF Standard, not PDF Print)
Mobile testing guidance (test on actual phone, bright sunlight readability)
References 2026 performance data by dimension

test_cases.name: Pre-Publication Quality Check
test_cases.description: User has completed carousel and needs validation before posting
test_cases.prompt: I've created my carousel on the 5-C framework for positioning. Before I post, can you review it and tell me if it meets best practices? I have 9 slides, headlines are specific, and design is consistent.
expected_outputs: Should ask for carousel content (headlines or description) to evaluate
Should provide comprehensive quality checklist
Should validate: slide count (5-10, 9 is good), headline specificity, design consistency
Should check: text density (30 words max per slide), narrative flow, hook strength
Should reference: mobile readiness, color contrast, one focal point per slide
Should evaluate CTA clarity and save-ability
Should provide pre-publication validation score/summary
success_criteria: Provides multi-section checklist (content, design, technical, engagement)
Evaluates headline specificity and scanability (2-second rule)
Checks slide count is optimal (9 is in sweet spot 5-10 range)
Validates one idea per slide
Confirms design consistency across slides
Checks if framework is named/reusable (saveable content)
Provides specific feedback, not generic approval
References engagement benchmarks (framework carousels get X% saves)

test_cases.name: Weak Hook Diagnosis
test_cases.description: User gets poor engagement and wants to understand why
test_cases.prompt: My carousel about LinkedIn tips only got 50 impressions. The first slide just says 'LinkedIn Tips for Success' with a swipe arrow. Why didn't it perform?
expected_outputs: Should identify weak hook as primary problem (determines 80% of engagement)
Should explain genericness (not specific enough to earn swipe)
Should provide specific hook alternatives with data backing
Should reference 2026 performance data on generic vs specific
Should explain what makes a hook 'earn the swipe'
Should provide corrected hook formula examples
Should estimate improvement from hook optimization
success_criteria: Clearly identifies hook as #1 reason for failure
Explains why 'LinkedIn tips' doesn't work (not specific, no value promise)
Provides specific alternatives: '5 LinkedIn tactics that generated 500 leads' format
References research: specific claims beat generic advice
Explains swipe-earning formula (promise, stat, question, challenge)
Provides before/after examples
Mentions that hook determines ~80% of performance
Offers testing strategy (rewrite hook, repost, compare)

test_cases.name: Text Wall Problem Diagnosis
test_cases.description: User has content but slides are text-heavy
test_cases.prompt: I have great content about my sales methodology but each slide has about 100 words. People aren't finishing. What's wrong?
expected_outputs: Should identify text density as major problem
Should reference 5-second rule (if slide takes >5 sec to read, users scroll)
Should recommend 30-word maximum per slide
Should explain algorithm impact (dwell time matters)
Should provide solution: split content across more slides
Should explain one-idea-per-slide principle
Should calculate new slide count needed for content density fix
success_criteria: Clearly identifies text walls as #1 reason for drop-off
References 5-second rule backed by 2026 research
Recommends maximum 30 words per slide (specific number, not vague)
Explains why this matters algorithmically (dwell time, completion rate)
Recommends splitting 100-word content across multiple slides
Provides specific restructuring guidance (one concept per slide)
Estimates new slide count (likely 10-12 slides from current 5-6)
References completion rate improvement if density reduced

test_cases.name: Timing & Posting Workflow
test_cases.description: User has completed carousel and ready to post
test_cases.prompt: My carousel is ready to go live on LinkedIn. When should I post it? What's the step-by-step process for uploading to LinkedIn?
expected_outputs: Should recommend best timing (Tuesday-Wednesday, 10 AM-12 PM local)
Should explain timing rationale backed by 2026 data
Should provide step-by-step upload workflow
Should include caption formula
Should reference importance of first 30 minutes (engagement velocity)
Should provide post-publish monitoring strategy
Should explain metrics to track (saves most important)
success_criteria: Recommends Tuesday-Wednesday with supporting data
Recommends 10 AM-12 PM with specific reason (peak professional browsing)
Provides exact LinkedIn steps: Start post > Document > Upload PDF > Title > Caption > Post
Provides caption formula and example
Explains first-30-minutes critical window
Recommends commenting on own post if slow start (increases momentum)
Lists metrics in order of importance: Saves, Dwell time, Comments, Shares, Clicks
Mentions benchmark: 15-20 sec dwell time target

test_cases.name: Performance Iteration Strategy
test_cases.description: User wants to understand which metrics matter most and how to improve
test_cases.prompt: My carousel got 2% engagement rate. How does that compare to benchmarks? What should I focus on improving for my next carousel?
expected_outputs: Should compare to 2026 benchmarks (6.60% average for carousels)
Should explain variance by audience size, content type, niche
Should identify save rate as most important metric (not likes)
Should explain algorithmic weight of metrics (saves 5x likes)
Should provide iteration strategy based on performance
Should ask diagnostic questions (hook strength, text density, CTA clarity)
Should reference framework-based content typically gets higher saves
success_criteria: Provides 2026 benchmark: 6.60% average for carousels (user at 2% = below average)
Explains that 2% could indicate: weak hook, text walls, unclear CTA, or niche factors
Emphasizes saves over likes (5x more valuable in algorithm)
References save rate benchmark: 5-10% of engaged users save top-performing carousels
Provides diagnostic questions: Was hook specific? Slide count? Text density? CTA clarity?
Suggests A/B testing (rewrite hook, reduce text, clarify CTA)
Explains framework vs narrative vs contrarian typically drives different save rates
Recommends testing on 4-8 carousel posts before changing strategy

test_cases.name: Format Rotation Guidance
test_cases.description: User wants to know if they should diversify beyond carousels
test_cases.prompt: I'm planning my LinkedIn content for next month. Should I post only carousels since they perform best, or mix in other formats?
expected_outputs: Should explain format rotation strategy (don't repeat same format)
Should reference algorithm penalties for format repetition (up to 20% penalty)
Should explain performance hierarchy: Carousels > Text+Image > Video > Text-only
Should provide rotation strategy recommendation
Should explain when to use each format
Should reference format rotation engagement benefits (37% more follower growth)
Should balance consistency (algorithm learns patterns) with variety
success_criteria: Explains format rotation necessity (algorithm penalizes repetition up to 20%)
References 2026 data: carousels best, but rotation beats repetition
Provides suggested rotation: Carousel > Text+Image > Video > Poll (weekly)
Explains rationale for each format: Carousels for saves, Text+Image for reach, Video for trust
References benefits: 37% more follower growth with rotation, 28% more consistent visibility
Recommends: 1-2 core formats (carousels) + variety every week
Explains algorithm learning (prefers format discipline) vs engagement (rewards variety)
Provides sustainable content mix guidance
